description: §4.12.2 — a nested `<program name= route=>` declares a SERVER ENDPOINT at the given route. That codegen is Nominal/spec-ahead, so the declaration fails closed with E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL and the compiler emits NEITHER a `new Worker(...)` reference NOR a bundle. Pre-fix (S356) `route=` was not implemented at all AND was silently mis-compiled: the extraction pre-pass claimed the program as a §4.12.4 web worker and emitted `new Worker("<base>.api.worker.js")` against a 71-byte stub. So the SPEC's "declares the nested program as a server endpoint" was a claim with no compiler behind it, presenting to the author as a client-side worker.
rationale: §4.12.2's attribute table gives `route=` as valid in nested position with the semantics "Declares the nested program as a server endpoint at the given route" — a shape the §4.12.3 execution-context table does not enumerate, and one nothing implements. §4.12.3 normative (S356) requires the inline-worker context be selected ONLY by `name=` with none of `lang=`/`mode=`/`route=`/`db=`/`port=`, and requires an unimplemented context to emit neither a reference nor a stand-in artifact and to fail closed naming the context.
